title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government outlines its response to the Committee's 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, detailing commitments to strengthen AI regulation, promote transparency, and safeguard public interests. It also outlines plans to collaborate with stakeholders, invest in research, and implement safeguards to ensure AI systems are safe, trustworthy, and aligned with societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has issued a policy outlining how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, aiming to maintain fairness, transparency, and exam integrity. The approach, requested by the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade, will set clear guidelines, monitor AI tools, and work with exam boards and educators to ensure reliable assessment.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how AI systems rely on copyrighted works and evaluates the legal and ethical implications of this practice. It offers an impact assessment and provides policy recommendations to balance innovation with copyright protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a formal response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” acknowledging the urgent need to address AI challenges. It outlines specific policy measures and commitments aimed at strengthening regulation, fostering innovation, and ensuring national security while promoting responsible AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence should be governed within public standards, detailing the topics to be examined and the procedures to be followed. It also includes a list of frequently asked questions to clarify key terms and expectations for stakeholders.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of Artificial Intelligence. The submission outlines key concerns and offers recommendations for improving AI governance.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document discusses how artificial intelligence is influencing the rules governing medical products, aiming to incorporate the AI White Paper's guidance. It outlines practical steps to ensure that AI-driven medical devices meet safety, efficacy, and transparency standards while fostering innovation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the defense organization the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user in the world for its size. It focuses on adopting AI technologies to improve operational capabilities while maintaining high standards of ethics and trust.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness AI opportunities and drive innovation. It also outlines measures to identify and mitigate the risks that come with using AI in transport.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyrighted works are used to train and improve AI systems, assessing compliance with legal standards and industry practices. It also highlights recent developments, challenges, and policy recommendations under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
